title: fix(doctor): retain interrupted capture publication evidence
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recovery discovery hiding healthy captures, and standalone Doctor retirement deleting interrupted captures, when publication stops after creating the destination but before removing the source name.

Closes #166246. Closes #166466.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already received [fs-safe 0.24.2](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.24.2) through #166457. Both pre-repair publication sites now call fs-safe directly, removing the duplicate unsupported-rename adapter introduced by #166425. Native `auto` owns the exclusive link/unlink fallback; `require` remains fail-closed.

A remaining `manifest.json.partial` means publication is incomplete. Discovery lists it beside healthy captures without granting a sealed manifest reference; baseline reuse and forward-resolution validation refuse it; automatic retirement retains it. This applies equally to exact hard-link pairs, copied finals from the earlier adapter, and contradictory names. No name is removed and no pair is accepted as a restore point. Snapshot/payload pairs without a manifest remain incomplete evidence. Existing manifest digests, scope, directory identity, outcome binding, payload integrity, and hard-link rejection remain in force.

## User Impact

Doctor can retain pre-repair captures on Linux filesystems that reject `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, using the upstream fallback. Interrupted captures remain available for manual inspection instead of disappearing from discovery or being deleted after 30 days. Ordinary expired sealed standalone captures keep their existing retirement policy. No configuration, database schema, or capture format changes are needed.

Thanks @MertBasar0 for the reproduction and recovery-window analysis.

## Evidence

- Verified all eight fs-safe 0.24.2 packages on npm; current main has all 13 direct pins and seven native platform locks at that version. All 104 generated npm lock mirrors pass, preserving platform constraints.
- Before the repair, the retirement regression deleted all three interrupted manifest fixtures; discovery/reuse/forward-binding regressions produced six failures.
- After the repair, `pnpm test src/infra/update-database-backup.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/status.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 52 tests (366.45 seconds including compiled-worker preparation). The regression states cover both manifest and snapshot/payload link windows, copied finals, and mismatched names. Existing symlink, external-hardlink, scope, and binding refusals remain covered.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- `pnpm changed:lanes --json`: core, core tests, documentation. `pnpm check:changed` passed, including core typechecking, all 27 test typecheck groups, full core lint, dead-export scans, runtime import cycles, and the applicable guards.
- The first CI attempt found missing braces in the new branches. The behavior-preserving follow-up passed targeted lint and independent review. Exact-head [CI run 37586605131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37586605131) is fully green at `0e6d3975d38084f1850588f3f950a56919f89215`; no admin exception is needed.
- Linux proof passed on a task-owned Colima VM (Ubuntu 24.04.4, Linux 6.8.0-117 aarch64, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.5.1) after AWS admission was unavailable. The syscall probe confirmed `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` returns `EINVAL`, while plain `renameat2`, `rename`, and `link` succeed.
- Actual `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 and printed `Pre-repair state retained for manual recovery at …/manifest.json` in every case below. Every payload SHA-256 and size matched the manifest; successful publication left one link and no partial manifest.

| Doctor state | Control | Selective seccomp EINVAL |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh state | pass, 19.16 s | pass, 19.82 s |
| Existing shared SQLite database | pass, 17.12 s | pass, 19.37 s |

- Real post-link/pre-unlink filesystem states were reconstructed from a Doctor capture: an exact manifest pair aged beyond 30 days, a SQLite snapshot/payload pair without a manifest, and a distinct-inode manifest pair. Running Doctor retirement and `openclaw update status --json` retained all bytes, inodes, and link counts; all three appeared as incomplete without recovery references, while two healthy sealed captures stayed visible.
- On an XFS loop mount, real `copyPluginSourceFile` captured and hashed 64 MiB through the copied descriptor in 3.55 s. `strace` recorded successful `FICLONE`; inodes differed (131/132), free space was unchanged at cloning, and destination mutation left source bytes unchanged while the remaining extents stayed shared. The mount was released.
- Exact-head CI also passed Doctor rehearsal (2 tests), fleet preflight (6), update/schema admission (18), and post-update recovery (40). The three additional manifest-parser, recovery-guidance, and directory-durability suites passed locally after a combined runtime importer invocation was refused before tests by the managed-Gateway artifact fence. That refusal was not bypassed.
- The canonical published-driver Docker cell passed: published `2026.9.8` → exact candidate head `0e6d3975d380`, update exit 0 in 650.837 s, finished state, readiness HTTP 200, running version verified, and durable/incognito session postchecks passed. The original 1125-second envelope was retained. The informational publication-recovery command did not indicate a failure. The released driver lacks modern original-capture lineage, so its documented missing-lineage notice remains; the standalone Doctor capture cases above all succeeded. Candidate tarball integrity/import-graph checks passed; SHA-256 `b0e1cdb3109c1151e147f3f119ca8eae01869301761016d6543eaa38b06f42e9`.
- Total selected consumer coverage: 170 passing tests across nine capture, recovery, Doctor, manifest, and durability files. Docker workload cleanup and XFS unmount completed. The task-owned VM and its container data were removed. No AWS lease was allocated.
- Production LOC: +55/−58 (net −3); tests +105/−96 (net +9). The 43-line retry adapter and its 77-line implementation-specific suite are removed.

| Release change | Consumer audit |
| --- | --- |
| fs-safe#843 exclusive-publication fallback | Direct use at both capture sites; duplicate fallback removed; interrupted evidence retained conservatively. |
| fs-safe#844 readable native clone descriptors | Plugin capture already hashes `copied.fd`; no call-site change needed. Real XFS clone and copied-descriptor hashing proof passed. |
